notes:
Top-line: large freight operator, global hubs + EU data residency constraints. Interested in Redwood Dedicated for steady, low-jitter inference for both customer-facing chat (ETA/status) and internal route optimization.

- From AE call (Sana) 2026-01-15: "We need guaranteed throughput during peak load windows (Americas morning -> EU afternoon)." Wants committed GPUs, predictable cost.
- Security: SOC2 mandatory, SSO via SAML + SCIM, KMS for key management, strict retention & egress policies for EU shipments.
- Workload mix: ~70% short chat/queries (avg seq 64 tokens), 30% long optimization runs (avg seq 1024 tokens) that run as batched jobs.
- Current telemetry (customer supplied): baseline 120 QPS for chat, steady token/sec ~7k-9k, observed daily spikes up to 480 QPS (peak 10-12 min bursts during morning routing churn).
- Model preference: open models verified in Redwood catalog (70B quantized for long jobs, 13B/Chat-optimized models for low latency chat). Want autoscaled fallback to smaller variant under degraded capacity.
- P95 latency target: chat < 200ms; p99 < 400ms for short queries. Optimization job throughput target: sustained tokens/sec targets for batched runs; can tolerate higher latency but want throughput guarantees.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high — willing to commit to 1yr reserved capacity with ramp if Redwood shows 25-30% cost advantage over self-hosting after quantization & batching gains.

Notes on procurement & SLA:
- Legal requested draft SLA showing uptime, p95 latency SLOs, credits model for breaches. Also need model verification / reproducibility clause for critical routing outputs.
- Finance: requires estimated ARR range for procurement approval and invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly).
